attributes.provenance: discovered live during the 2026-08-31 symbol-adoption pass (work_claim.symbol-adoption.20260831.v1): two of sounds_evt.c's 16 exact-gap candidates (fn_8009FCA8->DoAudioTallySFX, AudioPlayerPoison->AudioPlayerSeverePain) named an Xbox function whose name was ALREADY assigned to a different, previously-verified function elsewhere in the SAME TU. Both were adopted, then caught by a 'multiply-defined' mwld link error on the very next full ninja build, then reverted (see attempt.symbol-adoption-tupass.20260831.v1 for the full narrative).
attributes.scope: gdlmem.py symaudit's positional/LIS-anchored candidate generation (any TU, any pass); the underlying cause is generic to any name-reuse-blind rename source, not compiler-specific

subject: project:gdl
value: symaudit's exact-gap candidates are generated by positional (LIS-anchored) alignment against the Xbox PDB roster ALONE; they are not cross-checked against names already live elsewhere in the SAME TU or project. When the audit's anchoring drifts by even one slot near a cluster of adjacent same-purpose functions (confirmed 3x in the 2026-08-31 pass: two direct behavioral-contradiction cases in sounds_evt.c's fn_8009C378/fn_8009C3EC pair, plus two exact name collisions -- fn_8009FCA8 vs the pre-existing DoAudioTallySFX at a different address, and AudioPlayerPoison vs the pre-existing AudioPlayerSeverePain at a different address), a proposed candidate can silently name a DIFFERENT, already-real function. Static source verification (fnasm + caller/behavioral read) can miss this class of error entirely if the wrong-slot candidate still 'sounds plausible' for the target function; the two collisions in this pass were caught ONLY by the post-rename full-ninja build ('multiply-defined' mwld link error), not by any prior verification step. Consequence: (1) NEVER adopt a candidate without also grepping config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt for the exact candidate name to confirm it is not already assigned elsewhere before renaming; (2) treat the full-ninja GATE step as load-bearing even when per-candidate verification looked solid -- it is the only check that catches this class of error; (3) an adoption-support tool should perform this collision check automatically before ever surfacing a candidate (see also claim.law.symbol-rename-orphans-attempt-records for a second, structurally distinct build-breaking hazard from the same rename operation).
